2. The important facts of the case are that on 19.02.2018 at 05:00 p.m., the petitioner Dharmender Singh, the then Head Constable in Delhi Police, posted at PS Mayur Vihar, after finishing his duties was going to his home on motorcycle bearing no. DL5TC-0446 and when he reached near Red Light Signal, Balco Market, I.P. Extension, Delhi, all of a sudden, an Alto Maruti Car, bearing registration no. DL7CH- 2801 (in short "offending vehicle"), being driven by a female driver at a fast speed,

rashly and negligently, came from Chander Vihar side and without giving indicators, turned towards him and hit his motorcycle.
As a result, the petitioner fell down on the road along with his motorcycle and sustained injuries on his right leg.

He was taken to Max Hospital, Patparganj, Delhi,
where his MLC was prepared.
3. In connection with the accident, the petitioner got lodged the FIR no.58/2018, under sections 279/337 IPC at PS Madhu Vihar.

During the investigation, it was found that at the time of accident,
the offending vehicle was being driven by respondent no.1, owned by respondent no.2 and insured with respondent no.3.
After completion of the investigation, the present DAR was filed by the Investigating Agency.

Subsequently, the claim petition was also filed on behalf of the petitioner,
which was registered separately and was clubbed with the DAR matter vide order dated 08.12.2021.

sentences.text: All the respondents appeared at the time of filing of DAR.
The respondents were supplied with the copies of DAR and they filed their written-statements.
5. Respondent no.1 and 2 in their joint written-statement stated that the petitioner in collusion with the police, has falsely implicated them in this accident case.
Further, they stated that their vehicle was duly insured with respondent no.3 and hence, they are not liable to pay any compensation.

6. The respondent no.3/ insurance company submitted its reply on the format of legal offer by stating that "due to non-availability of attendance record, loss of pay and other relevant treatment papers, they are not in a position to make any offer at this stage".
7.

Upon completion of pleadings of the parties, vide order dated 28.07.2018, following issues were framed:
i).

Whether petitioner suffered injuries during the accident occurred on 19.02.2018 at about 05:00 p.m. at Balco Market, I.P. Extn., near Red Light Signal, due to rash and negligent driving of the vehicle bearing no. DL-7CH-2801, being driven by respondent no.1/ driver?
OPP ii).
Whether petitioners is entitled for compensation, if so, to what extent and from whom?

OPP iii). Relief.

My findings on the issues are as under:-

sentences.text: Before the issue under discussion can be decided in favour of the petitioner, the petitioner is required to prove at least on the balance of probability that in the accident in which he received injuries it was because of the vehicle bearing registration no. DL-7CH-2801 i.e., the offending vehicle, that it was being driven rashly or negligently by respondent no.1 on 19.02.2018 at about 05:00 p.m, at Balco Market, I.P. Extn., near Red Light Signal.

The balance of probability does not mean that any version of the accident or any vehicle alleged to be involved in the accident will have to be gullibly accepted by the Tribunal, but every material fact has to be proved by such proof and in such a manner by the petitioner that after considering the matters before it, the Tribubal either believes that it exists, or considers its existence so probable that a prudent man ought, under the circumstances of the particular case, to act upon the supposition that it exists.

12. The date of the accident in which the petitioner received injuries is that of 19.02.2018, whereas,
the FIR came to be registered on 25.02.2018.

Without there being any explanation on record as to how the registration number of the offending vehicle came to be mentioned in the complaint of the petitioner, dated 25.02.2018,
the delay in registration of FIR has to go adverse against the petitioner.

14. In the clarification given by the petitioner on 18.09.2024 before the Tribunal, the reason for delay could have been that the husband of the respondent no.1 was probably Inspector in the police department.
The Tribunal cannot take into consideration that explanation as it may be an afterthought as well having no connection with the truth.

15. In cross-examination of the petitioner recorded before the Court Commissioner on 17.05.2023 with respect to delay in the registration of FIR, the petitioner deposed that, "...On inquiry with the concerned police station Madhu Vihar, I was informed that the call has been filed as untraced.
Thereafter my wife had called on 100 number and narrated the incident and also mentioned the registration number of the offending vehicle.
It is correct that I did not convey the registration number of the alleged offending vehicle to my wife or relatives".

If the petitioner did not convey the registration number of the offending vehicle to his wife then the question which crops up is how the wife of the petitioner was in a position to convey the registration number of the offending vehicle to the police when the wife of the petitioner called on telephone 100 number?
There is no answer to that question in the record of the case.

It is further mentioned in the complaint that at that time from the place of accident, one Constable Vinod, who was posted at PS Preet Vihar, was going and he called on telephone number 100.
A PCR van got the petitioner admitted in Max Hospital.

In the cross-examination of the petitioner conducted before the Court Commissioner on 17.05.2023, the petitioner deposed that, "I noted down the registration number of the offending vehicle", whereas, it appeared by way of clarification sought on 18.09.2024 when petitioner stated before this Tribunal that he had seen the registration number of the offending vehicle and the same was mentioned in the FIR lodged on his complaint.

The petitioner further stated that when he was admitted in the Max Hospital, he had noted down the registration number of the offending vehicle on a piece of paper and when the Investigating Officer had come to take a statement at his home, he had given the registration number of the offending vehicle after reading the same from the piece of paper and the investigating officer of the case did not ask him to give that piece of paper on which the registration number of the vehicle was written.

20. From the clarification as given by the petitioner and what has been deposed to by the petitioner in his cross-examination quoted herein above, the case of the petitioner is that he did not memorise the registration number of the offending vehicle, rather he had noted down the registration number on a piece of paper.

When the Investigating Officer had come to take the statement of the petitioner,

sentences.text: 21. The petitioner has not produced or proved that piece of paper which would be primary evidence as far as the involvement of the motor vehicle is concerned.

As the petitioner has not produced the primary evidence (nor has led any secondary evidence to that effect regarding the piece of paper and the registration number of the offending vehicle mentioned on the piece of paper), the Tribunal does not know as to the fact if the registration number mentioned on the piece of paper was the same as that of the offending vehicle in the present case or it was some other number or alphabet mentioned on the piece of paper.

sentences.text: In the entire case, in the claim petition filed by the petitioner or in the DAR filed by the Investigating Officer, there is no foundation of what the petitioner had stated regarding coming of the PCR van and the offending vehicle being present and the PCR official noting down the registration number of the offending vehicle.

25. Assuming that whatever the petitioner stated before the Tribunal by way of clarification is true,
then it was incumbent upon the petitioner to examine relevant witness in order to prove the facts.

Without the proof of facts, the Tribunal would not assume that whatever facts by way of clarification the petitioner has stated before the Tribunal are proved facts which could be considered by this Tribunal for deciding the present case.

It may again be noted that the reason for the delay in the registration of FIR as stated by the petitioner on 18.09.2024 before this Tribunal i.e. the petitioner came to know that the husband of the respondent no.1 was probably the Inspector in police department because of which there was a delay in registration of FIR, has no foundation of any kind in the entire DAR/ claim petition, which is before this Tribunal.

In the light of discussion so far, it could be safely said that the petitioner has completely failed to prove even on the balance of probability that on the date of accident it was the offending vehicle which was involved or had caused the accident.

26. sentences.text:
29. It was not the case of the petitioner that he knew the respondent no.1 before the accident,
therefore, how the Investigating Officer has fixed the identity of the respondent no.1 being the driver of the offending vehicle remains in the realm of mystery.

The density of motor vehicles in a metropolitan area like Delhi is so much that if any fictitious registration number is told to police,
there is a possibility that such a motor vehicle could be traced out and if any injury is received by any person not even in a motor vehicular accident and such person alleges to have received injuries in the accident on a particular date, it is very much the possibilities that such vehicle would be traced to have been involved in the accident and concomitant result would be a claim petition against the owner/ driver and its insurance company for compensation.
30.

In the light of nature of evidence which is before this Tribunal, the facts which have been proved and the facts which ought to have been proved but not proved, it is not possible for the Tribunal to hold that the petitioner has been successful in proving all the material facts of the issue under discussion even on the balance of probability.

Merely, because an accident involving a motor vehicle has happened and before the Tribunal there is the injured and the respondents along with insurance company, it does not give the justification to allow the claim petition.

Before any claim petition is allowed, the Tribunal has to be satisfied that the yardstick of balance of probability which _____________________________________________________________________________ MACT no. 301/2018, Dharmender Singh v. Priyanka Aggarwal & Ors. 12 of 13 Pages is akin to saying like that the case of the petitioner is more likely to have happened than not on the basis of weighing of the evidence which is before the Tribunal and in the present case, the petitioner has failed to measure up to the said yardstick.

Accordingly, issue no.2 is decided against the petitioner and in favour of the Dar - Dharmender Singh vs Priyanka Agarwal on 8 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/61603225/
